item: A README explains what the project is and how to run it
rationale: Without instructions nobody else can rerun the work
reference: The Turing Way: Guide for Reproducible Research

rationale: Reuse of code and data requires permission stated in a licence
Credit and persistent identification of research software
reference: Software Citation Principles (Smith et al. 2016); FAIR4RS F1

item: The project is under version control
rationale: Records which version of the code produced which result
The analysis cannot run without knowing what it needs
New package versions can change results silently

item: A container or environment specification is provided (Dockerfile; devcontainer; Binder)
A single entry point or pipeline runs the analysis (Makefile; _targets.R; Snakefile; dvc.yaml; run_all)
rationale: Removes undocumented manual steps and their order

item: Continuous integration runs the code automatically
rationale: Detects breakage when code or dependencies change

item: Data are included or referenced by a persistent identifier or repository link
rationale: Results cannot be checked without the data

item: Data are documented (codebook; data dictionary; data README)
rationale: Variables must be understood to be reused

item: Code does not depend on absolute paths or setwd()
rationale: Absolute paths break on every other computer
reference: The Turing Way: Reproducible Research (portable code)

item: Random number seeds are set where randomness is used
rationale: Simulations and resampling give different results otherwise

item: No very large files are kept in the code repository
rationale: Large data belong in a data repository with an identifier
reference: The Turing Way: Version Control (large files)
